_note: Fixed demo story set (30 stories; the 6 science and technology stories were added 2026-10-23). ALL STORIES ARE FICTIONAL: events, people, quotes, companies and the transit authority are invented. Real neighborhoods and sports teams are used for flavor only. The summarizer must use only `facts` and `wire_text`. Field guide: importance 1-5; base_column_inches = length the story wants; hard_hitting_lean = how a Hard-hitting angle moves perceived lean (-1 left ... +1 right, 0 none; Puff moves it by -0.5x this value, Straight by 0); targets = entity ids (see districts.philly.json) that a Hard-hitting angle annoys; sensitivity 'high' = Puff angle not allowed, stricter summarizer prompt; storyline/storyline_step = continuing stories across days.

stories.wire_headline: Phillies take Game 1 of NLCS, 5-3
stories.wire_text: The Phillies beat their opponents 5-3 in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series on Tuesday night in South Philadelphia. Rookie shortstop Danny Ocasio drove in three runs, including a two-run double in the sixth inning. The announced crowd was 44,812. Game 2 is Thursday.

stories.wire_headline: Council budget committee backs closing Richmond Street branch library
stories.wire_text: A City Council budget committee voted 4-1 on Wednesday to recommend closing the Richmond Street branch library in Port Richmond to save an estimated $1.3 million a year. The branch logged about 52,000 visits last year. The full Council is expected to take up the recommendation next week. Committee members said the city must close a budget gap; the lone opposing member said the neighborhood was not consulted.

stories.wire_headline: Transit authority proposes 25-cent fare increase
stories.wire_text: The Philadelphia Transit Authority on Wednesday proposed raising the base fare by 25 cents, from $2.50 to $2.75, to help close a projected $64 million operating deficit. The authority's board will vote on the plan in three days. Officials said the increase would raise about $18 million a year and that service cuts remain under consideration if the deficit is not closed.

stories.wire_headline: Market pickle stand marks 100 years
stories.wire_text: DiNardo's Pickles, a stand at Reading Terminal Market, will celebrate its 100th anniversary on Saturday. The stand has been run by the same family for four generations and still uses a brine recipe written down in 1926. The owners plan to give away 1,000 free pickles at the celebration.

stories.wire_headline: West Philly community garden told to clear lot after sale to developer
stories.wire_text: Gardeners at the Cedar Avenue Community Garden in West Philadelphia have been given 60 days to leave the lot after it was sold to Penn Treaty Development Group for $2.1 million. About 80 households have plots at the garden, which has operated on the lot for 19 years. The developer plans a 48-unit apartment building and said it is open to discussing space for a smaller garden on site.

stories.wire_headline: Pennsylvania awarded $410 million in federal bridge repair grants
stories.wire_text: Pennsylvania will receive $410 million in federal grants to repair aging bridges, the U.S. Department of Transportation announced Wednesday. The state has more structurally deficient bridges than all but two other states. Philadelphia-area projects account for about $95 million of the total. Work on the first projects is expected to begin next spring.

stories.wire_headline: Water department tests sensors to predict sewer overflows
stories.wire_text: The city water department has installed 120 sensors in sewers along the Delaware River to test whether they can predict overflows during heavy rain. The two-year pilot costs $3.4 million, most of it from a state grant. The department said early data could help it warn residents up to two hours before an overflow.

stories.wire_text: The Philadelphia Union clinched a spot in the MLS playoffs with a 2-0 home win on Wednesday night. Midfielder Tomás Abara scored in the 34th minute and forward Kwame Lister added a second in the 81st. The Union have won five of their last six matches.

stories.wire_headline: Two killed, three injured in Hunting Park rowhouse fire
stories.wire_text: Two people were killed and three were injured in a rowhouse fire in Hunting Park early Thursday, the fire department said. Firefighters arrived about four minutes after the 2:40 a.m. call and brought the fire under control in roughly 30 minutes. Officials said smoke detectors in the home were not working. The cause is under investigation. The victims' names have not been released.

stories.wire_headline: Mayor's office proposes wage tax increase to close budget gap
stories.wire_text: The mayor's office on Thursday proposed raising the city wage tax by 0.2 percentage points for residents to help close a $90 million budget gap. The administration said the change would cost a resident earning $50,000 about $100 a year. The proposal needs City Council approval. Business groups said the increase would push employers out of the city; the administration said the alternative is deeper service cuts.

stories.wire_text: Transit Workers Local 412, which represents about 5,000 Philadelphia Transit Authority bus and train operators, said Thursday it will hold a strike vote if the authority's budget plan includes service cuts. stories.wire_headline: University City lab reports cheaper battery material; startup eyes Navy Yard plant
stories.wire_text: Researchers at a University City materials lab say they have made a battery electrode from iron and sulfur that costs about 40 percent less than current materials. The results have not yet been reviewed by other scientists. A startup formed by the researchers said it is considering a pilot plant at the Navy Yard that could employ about 60 people, but it has not raised the money to build it.

stories.wire_text: Helix Forge Therapeutics said Thursday it will add 400 jobs at the Navy Yard over the next two years as it expands manufacturing of a gene therapy treatment. stories.wire_headline: Six-story mural honoring city's jazz history unveiled on Ridge Avenue
stories.wire_text: A six-story mural celebrating Philadelphia's jazz history was unveiled Thursday on Ridge Avenue. The piece took 14 months to complete and involved more than 200 neighborhood volunteers. It depicts musicians playing in the clubs that once lined the avenue. The city's mural program funded the project.

stories.wire_headline: Volunteer sensors find 11-degree heat gap between neighborhoods
stories.wire_text: A volunteer project that placed 300 temperature sensors across the city found that the hottest blocks in North Philadelphia were up to 11 degrees warmer than tree-lined blocks in the Northwest on the same summer afternoons. Blocks with the least tree cover were the hottest. A city spokesperson said a tree-planting program is funded through next year and declined to comment on the findings until the full report is published.

stories.wire_text: A late-season heat wave pushed temperatures above 40 degrees Celsius in parts of Spain, Portugal and Greece this week, prompting water-use restrictions in all three countries. Officials in Greece said reservoirs near Athens are at their lowest October level in 30 years.

stories.wire_text: The Philadelphia Transit Authority board voted 6-3 on Friday to raise the base fare to $2.75, effective next month. A Council spokesperson said members would also consider reducing the branch's hours instead of closing it.

stories.wire_headline: City overdose deaths down 12 percent; Kensington still hardest hit
stories.wire_text: Overdose deaths in Philadelphia fell 12 percent in the first nine months of the year compared with the same period last year, according to a health department report released Friday. Kensington and surrounding neighborhoods still accounted for about a third of deaths. The department said it will add two mobile outreach vans that offer treatment referrals and overdose-reversal medication.

stories.wire_headline: Payroll vendor breach exposes data of 9,000 city workers
stories.wire_text: A software company that processes payroll for the city said Thursday that hackers accessed records belonging to about 9,000 city employees, including names and partial bank account numbers. The company said Social Security numbers were not taken. The city said it learned of the breach two weeks ago and is offering affected workers free credit monitoring for one year.

stories.wire_text: The Philadelphia Transit Authority and Transit Workers Local 412 reached a tentative agreement about 40 minutes before a 12:01 a.m. strike deadline, both sides said. Under the deal, the planned late-night service cuts are dropped and the fare increase will be phased in over two years instead of taking effect next month. Union members still must ratify the agreement.

stories.wire_headline: Councilmember proposes business tax cut for small firms
stories.wire_text: Councilmember Teresa Vance, who represents part of the Northeast, introduced a bill Monday to cut the city's business privilege tax for companies with less than $1 million in annual revenue. Her office estimates the cut would cost the city $22 million a year. Vance said it would help small businesses hire; budget officials said the city cannot afford it while facing a $90 million gap.

stories.wire_headline: State permit review delays former refinery redevelopment by six months
stories.wire_text: Redevelopment of the former refinery site in Southwest Philadelphia will be delayed at least six months while state regulators complete an additional environmental review of soil contamination, the developer said Monday. The project is expected to create about 1,200 construction jobs. State officials said the review is required because new soil samples showed higher contamination levels than earlier tests.

stories.wire_text: Enrollment in the city's public school district fell 3 percent this year, the district said Monday, and officials will study merging five under-enrolled schools. Applications to the city's charter schools rose 7 percent over the same period. The district said no decision will be made before a series of community meetings in the spring.

stories.wire_headline: New building permit software doubles approval times, contractors say
stories.wire_text: Contractors say a new online permit system launched by the city in August has roughly doubled the wait for routine building approvals, from about 15 business days to more than 30. A trade group representing 200 small builders said some members have laid off workers while waiting. The city's licensing department said the backlog is shrinking and that most problems came from the switch from the old system.

stories.wire_headline: Filipino-Italian restaurant opens on East Passyunk
stories.wire_text: Chef Marco Dizon opened Lola's Table, a Filipino-Italian restaurant, on East Passyunk Avenue this weekend. The 40-seat restaurant serves dishes such as adobo-braised short rib with polenta. Dizon, who grew up in the neighborhood, said the menu is based on meals at his grandmother's house. Reservations are booked for the next three weeks.
